definitions.explanation: A person employed to do household work or attend to the needs of a master or household. In modern usage, primarily appears in historical, literary, or fantasy contexts.

examples.japanese: {王|おう}は{召使|めしつか}いを{呼|よ}んだ。
{屋敷|やしき}には{何人|なんにん}もの{召使|めしつか}いがいた。
examples.english: There were many servants in the mansion.

examples.japanese: {昔|むかし}の{貴族|きぞく}は{大勢|おおぜい}の{召使|めしつか}いに{囲|かこ}まれて{暮|く}らしていた。
examples.english: Nobles of old lived surrounded by many servants.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{召使|めしつか}いを{雇|やと}う (hire a servant)
・{召使|めしつか}いを{呼|よ}ぶ (call a servant)
・{忠実|ちゅうじつ}な{召使|めしつか}い (a loyal servant)

Derived from {召|め}し{使|つか}う (to employ, to summon and use). In contemporary Japanese, this word is mostly found in historical dramas, period novels, fairy tales, and fantasy settings. For modern domestic workers, {家事|かじ}ヘルパー or {家政婦|かせいふ} are used instead.
